label: Kubernetes

corePack.why: CrashLoopBackOff is the kubelet saying a container never stays up.
corePack.whyNow: Workloads in backoff look Running on coarse dashboards.
corePack.metric: Pods in CrashLoopBackOff and time in backoff

corePack.why: API server latency is control-plane user experience for every kubectl and controller.
corePack.whyNow: Slow apiserver precedes failed deploys and NotReady flaps.
corePack.metric: Apiserver request latency by verb and resource

corePack.why: Node NotReady starts the eviction clock for every pod on that worker.
corePack.whyNow: You need blast radius before default tolerationSeconds elapse.
corePack.metric: Nodes Ready=false and pods at risk

corePack.why: OOMKilled and eviction are memory-limit and node-pressure failures, not generic restarts.
corePack.whyNow: Limit misses and MemoryPressure need different owners.

corePack.why: If the log pipeline is dropping, every cluster alert is flying blind.
corePack.whyNow: Buffer overflow is a silent observability outage.
corePack.metric: Fluent Bit / Fluentd buffer overflow and retry exhaustion

corePack.why: Expired kubelet or apiserver certs take the cluster offline on a calendar.
corePack.whyNow: Certificate expiry is scheduled and preventable.

corePack.why: Control-plane health (apiserver, etcd, scheduler, controller-manager) is the cluster itself.
corePack.whyNow: Worker symptoms are downstream of control-plane loss.

valueHypothesis: Kubernetes monitoring should start with crashloop, apiserver latency, node NotReady, OOMKilled, the log pipeline, and certificates—the failure modes Kubernetes itself documents—not Docker-only OOM or incidental audit mentions.
rationale: Kubernetes debug and SRE practice start with workload restarts, node Ready, apiserver SLOs, OOM/eviction, pipeline health, and certificates. UC-3.2.47 exists so OOMKilled is not omitted.
